inputs.fx_note: fx_rate = HKD per CNY = 1 / 0.8513 (Yahoo HKDCNY=X 0.8513 at 2026-10-11T02:32Z; 1-month range 0.851-0.856). All flows, net cash and per-share values are computed in CNY and converted to HKD at 1.1747 so intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are comparable to the HKD quote. Parity check: HK$3.62 x 0.8513 = RMB3.08/share; FY2025 diluted EPS RMB0.338 -> P/E 9.1x, consistent with the HK-press P/E of ~9-10x. No dual listing exists for a direct parity check.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z regular close (HKEX), Yahoo chart API; latest trading session before the 2026-10-11 valuation date
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares H1 FY2026 (2,218.0m basic + 38.1m share-option dilution = 2,256.1m), interim report note 11. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The only buyback was RMB187.0m in FY2021; zero since, so the flat count is a modelling convention, not something the company is funding with repurchases (option exercises add ~1%/yr of shares, which the SBC charge stands in for).
inputs.cash_composition: 30 Jun 2026 interim balance sheet: cash and equivalents 1,452.890 + time deposits 494.402 + FVTPL other financial assets 1,488.029 (structured deposits 1,079.852, not principal-protected; unquoted fund investments 408.177 at level-3 fair value) + entrusted loan to a related party at amortised cost 80.000 = RMB3,515.3m. No bank borrowings. Final FY2025 dividend (RMB578.9m) already paid in H1 2026; no interim dividend declared, so no declared-unpaid distribution to deduct.
inputs.wacc_rationale: CNY-built cost of equity, no financial debt (leases are in the flows under treatment B): China 10-year CGB ~1.8% + beta 1.15 x 6.7% ERP (mature-market ERP plus China country premium) = ~9.5%. No ad-hoc regulatory premium: education-policy and demographic risk are carried by the 25% bear weight and its declining-enrolment path, not stacked on the discount rate. Same WACC in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. lease_cost_pct_path charges the full lease cash payment (FY2025: principal 249.423 + interest 110.107 = 359.53, 7.8% of revenue; both read off the FY2025 cash flow statement, financing section) inside EBIT. Lease liabilities (1,459.6 at 30 Jun 2026: 279.4 current + 1,180.2 non-current) are EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A path is property-and-equipment depreciation only (FY2025 331.1 = 7.2% of revenue); right-of-use depreciation (266.3) is excluded so the lease is not charged twice in cash-tax EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest; profit is substantially all attributable to owners of the Company.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US adaptations. China East Education is an operating company -- B2C vocational training (culinary, auto services, IT, western pastry, beauty) across 233 schools/centres -- with no lending book, no investment-property model and no live corporate action, so the routing table sends it to owner-FCF. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). OWNER FCF: reported FCF (OCF 1,555.8 - PP&E purchases 583.6 = 972.2) - SBC 18.6 - lease cash 359.5 = 594.1 (FY2025). Interest income is NOT deducted from reported FCF because this filer classifies interest received in INVESTING activities and adjusts interest income out of OCF (cash flow statement lines 'Interest income from time deposits and bank balances (48,193)' and 'Interest received ... 70,606' under investing) -- deducting it again would double-strip. The EBITDA margin path is built ex interest income (51.7) and ex FVTPL fair-value gains (47.0): FY2025 reported EBITDA 1,691.9 - 51.7 - 47.0 = 1,593.2 = 34.5% of revenue (post-IFRS 16, before lease cash). Both income streams' source assets (cash, time deposits, structured deposits, funds, entrusted loan) are in the bridge at book/fair value (matching-asset rule). FY0 component check: 34.5% EBITDA - 0.4% SBC - 7.8% lease - 7.2% D&A = 19.1% EBIT; x (1-23%) + D&A - capex 12.8% + WC on +498 revenue at 30% = ~RMB560m vs 594 actual owner FCF -- ties within non-cash FX/disposal noise. WORKING CAPITAL: prepaid-tuition model; contract liabilities rose 231.6 on +498 revenue in FY2025 and 138.9 on +137 in FY2024; total WC release 135.7 (27% of revenue change) in FY2025, so wc_capture 30% on the CHANGE in revenue, which turns into an outflow automatically in bear years with falling revenue. CASH TAX: FY2025 income tax 228.3 on PBT 984.4 = 23.2%; cash taxes paid 216.9; FY2024 cash rate was a low 15% (paid 99.9 on 654.4). 23% flat; some schools enjoy preferential/exempt status but the group rate has run 22-26% on the P&L. CAPEX: FY2025 PP&E 583.6 + net leasehold-land deposits 7.7 = 12.8% of revenue; H1 FY2026 PP&E 328.5 + land 55.3 net = 15.3% (industrial-park build: Jiangxi land acquired, RMB261m contracted commitments at 30 Jun 2026). Base glides 14% -> 9% as the park programme completes, still above P&E depreciation so terminal growth is funded. BUYBACKS: none since FY2021 (RMB187.0m). SBC is small (0.4% of revenue, falling) but not zero, so the house/street band is narrow but defined. PRICE CONTEXT: stock is near the bottom of its 52-week range (HK$3.505-7.21) after sliding from ~HK$4.5-5.1 mid-year; H1 FY2026 interim showed revenue +10.6% but OCF down 9.5% YoY, selling expenses up to RMB568m from RMB491m, and no interim dividend.

equity_bridge.item: Operating cash requirement (~10% of FY2025 revenue)
equity_bridge.note: The cash pile funds RMB1.88bn of prepaid tuition (contract liabilities, 30 Jun 2026) and seasonal payroll/lease outflows; treating every renminbi as surplus would overstate distributable value. Haircut equals ~1.2 months of revenue.

equity_bridge.item: H1 FY2026 owner FCF already inside 30 Jun 2026 cash
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 FCF 373.5 - SBC 6.4 - lease cash 169.1 (117.8 principal + 51.4 interest) = 198.0. The June balance sheet already holds it and year 1 of the DCF (FY2026) counts it again; deducted once here to avoid the overlap.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.4% 5yr, 2.6% 3yr) diverges far more than 30% from revenue (4.8%/6.5%) and EPS (24.5%/26.5%). Book value is flat because the company pays out most earnings as dividends (RMB443m FY2025, RMB579m paid H1 FY2026) -- equity growth is a payout artefact, not a growth signal. EPS CAGR is inflated by a depressed FY2020-23 base (COVID closures, campus build-out). Revenue 3yr CAGR used as the anchor; FY2026 guidance is >10%.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - lease principal - lease interest (interest income already outside OCF for this filer). Owner FCF was negative FY2021-23 during the peak campus/industrial-park capex cycle (capex 18-25% of revenue) and the 2022 lockdowns; the 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is undefined from a negative base. The 5yr owner-FCF CAGR (13.7%) exceeds reported (4.5%) because SBC (76.2 -> 18.6) and lease cash (390.6 -> 359.5) both FELL while revenue grew -- the opposite of the usual SBC-outgrowing-cash-flow warning.

base.narrative: FY2026 meets the >10% revenue guidance (H1 +10.6%), then growth fades to 2% as industrial-park capacity fills and the shrinking school-leaver cohort bites. EBITDA margin holds ~35.5% (FY2025 34.5%) -- gross-margin gains from the mix shift to long-term programmes are largely spent on rising advertising. Capex steps down from the park build (14%) to ~9% maintenance-plus.

bull.narrative: Policy tailwind (2024-2035 education outline, 2026 MoE emerging-field programmes) plus technician-college upgrades lift fees and enrolment: high-single-digit growth for five years as the parks in Anhui, Sichuan, Shandong, Guizhou, Henan, Jiangsu and Jiangxi fill, and new AI/robotics/elder-care/NEV majors widen the funnel. Operating leverage on fixed staff and campus costs takes EBITDA margin to 38%, and lease cost falls as owned park campuses replace leased sites.

bear.narrative: The shrinking youth cohort and the 'intensified regional competition' the Chairman already flags turn enrolment down from FY2028; advertising keeps rising to defend intake, so EBITDA margin falls back to 28% (between FY2023's ~26% and FY2024's ~30%). Fixed campus leases on a shrinking base push lease cost to 8.5% of revenue. Capex is cut to maintenance, and falling revenue unwinds prepaid tuition (WC outflow). A tightening of private-vocational licensing, fee or advertising rules -- the 2021 tutoring crackdown is the precedent -- would land here.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 meets the >10% revenue guidance (H1 +10.6%), then growth fades to 2% as industrial-park capacity fills and the shrinking school-leaver cohort bites. EBITDA margin holds ~35.5% -- mix-driven gross-margin gains are largely spent on rising advertising (selling expenses ~23% of revenue). Capex steps down from the park build to ~9% of revenue. The large net-cash position (RMB3.5bn, ~45% of market cap) is a meaningful floor.
scenario_narratives.bull: Vocational training stays explicitly policy-favoured and the company's technician-college upgrades and new-sector majors (AI, humanoid robotics, elder care, NEV) lift both enrolment and fee per student; high-single-digit growth for five years and operating leverage to a 38% EBITDA margin. Analyst targets (Citi HK$7.8, CICC HK$9.5) sit in this case.
scenario_narratives.bear: Demographics and regional competition win: enrolment declines from FY2028, advertising keeps rising, margin falls back to 28% and fixed leases deleverage on a shrinking base; any regulatory tightening of private vocational schools lands here. Net cash still carries a large share of the value, so the bear case is a de-rating, not a solvency event.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default: single-regulator dependency (China private education, with the 2021 tutoring crackdown as precedent) and a structurally shrinking student cohort. Base 50%: guidance and H1 delivery support the near-term path. Bull cut to 25% from 35% because it needs enrolment growth against demographics, sustained margin expansion despite rising ad spend, and continued policy support all at once.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF in CNY, converted to HKD at the spot rate. Leases are an operating cost (full cash payment inside EBIT), so lease liabilities stay out of net debt; interest and fair-value income are excluded from the flows and their source assets (RMB3.5bn of cash, deposits, structured deposits and funds) are added in the bridge, less an operating-cash reserve and the H1 FY2026 cash overlap. Terminal value is capped at 12x to reflect the demographic ceiling on a mature Chinese education business.
key_risks_to_valuation: Regulatory: an abrupt change in China's rules for private vocational schools (licensing, fees, advertising, for-profit status) -- the 2021 K-12 tutoring precedent
Demographics: shrinking school-leaver cohort compresses the addressable pool for long-term programmes
Customer acquisition cost: selling expenses rising faster than revenue (H1 FY2026 RMB568m vs RMB491m)
Treasury quality: RMB1.08bn of structured deposits are not principal-protected and RMB408m of unquoted funds are level-3 fair values; both are taken at carrying value in the bridge
Capital allocation: industrial-park capex could stay elevated (H1 FY2026 15% of revenue) rather than taper as modelled
Cayman/VIE-style holding structure and HKD/CNY translation risk for HKD shareholders
